messages.content:
Given a question and an answer, analyze the complexity of each sentence in the answer. Break down each sentence into one or more fully understandable statements. Ensure that no pronouns are used in any statement. Format the outputs in JSON.
Please return the output in a JSON format that complies with the following schema as specified in JSON Schema:
{"properties": {"statements": {"description": "The generated statements", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Statements", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["statements"], "title": "StatementGeneratorOutput", "type": "object"}Do not use single quotes in your response but double quotes,properly escaped with a backslash.

--------EXAMPLES-----------
Example 1
Input: {
    "question": "Who was Albert Einstein and what is he best known for?",
    "answer": "He was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time. He was best known for developing the theory of relativity, he also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
}
Output: {
    "statements": [
        "Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist.",
        "Albert Einstein is recognized as one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time.",
        "Albert Einstein was best known for developing the theory of relativity.",
        "Albert Einstein also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
    ]
}
-----------------------------

Now perform the same with the following input
input: {
    "question": "user: What is the significance of CIS's reverse proxy?\nassistant: The significance of CIS's reverse proxy is that it can compress and decompress content, allowing it to convert between compressed and uncompressed formats independently of caching. This means that it can pull content from a customer's origin server via gzip and serve it to clients uncompressed, or vice versa. Additionally, CIS's reverse proxy can handle multiple types of compression, including gzip and brotli, and can also handle requests that may otherwise cause errors, such as those with the Accept-Encoding header, which is not respected and is removed.\nuser: How to Brotli compression\nassistant: To enable Brotli compression in CIS, follow these steps:\n1. Log in to your CIS account.\n2. Choose the appropriate domain.\n3. Click the Performance tab.\n4. Click the Advanced tab.\n5. Toggle the Brotli switch to On.\nCIS returns gzip or brotli encoded responses to compatible clients and browsers for the following content-types:\n\ntext/html text/richtext text/plain text/css text/x-script text/x-component text/x-java-source text/x-markdown application/javascript application/x-javascript text/javascript text/js image/x-icon image/vnd.microsoft.icon application/x-perl application/x-httpd-cgi text/xml application/xml application/xml+rss application/vnd.api+json application/x-protobuf application/json multipart/bag multipart/mixed application/xhtml+xml font/ttf font/otf font/x-woff image/svg+xml application/vnd.ms-fontobject application/ttf\nuser: reverse proxy with webP\nassistant: CIS's reverse proxy is capable of converting between compressed and uncompressed formats, including WebP. WebP is a modern image format providing superior lossless and lossy compression for images.  WebP conversion does not change the image URL, and the Content-Type HTTP header is used to tell the browser the original format of an image. To ensure WebP is not served from cache to a browser lacking WebP support, it's recommended to disable WebP at your origin web server when using image size optimization.\nWhen image size optimization is active, it adds the following headers to image requests that are compressed:\n* cf-bgj: imgq:85\n* cf-polished: qual=85, origFmt=jpeg, origSize=95005\n* cf-cache-status: HIT\nThe cf-bgj header confirms that CIS applied image size optimization and returns the image quality setting (imgq). The cf-polished header represents the image size optimization status and returns the image quality setting (qual) and original size (origSize). The cf-cache-status confirms that the image has been cached and image size optimization can be applied.\nuser:  With a Free Trial Plan, why I cannot create an instance?\nassistant: With the Free Trial Plan for IBM Cloud® Internet Services (CIS), you are only allowed to have one instance per account for the lifetime of the account. If you already have a free trial instance, if you delete a free trial instance, or if the free trial expires, you are not allowed to create another free trial instance. \nuser: gertting so slow, isn't CIS supported for DDos?\nassistant: Yes, IBM Cloud Internet Services (CIS) does provide protection against DDoS attacks.  A distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack is a malicious attempt to disrupt normal traffic of a server, service, or network by overwhelming the target or its surrounding infrastructure with a flood of internet traffic, and the effectiveness of this protection can depend on various factors such as the type and scale of the attack. However, it might be due to other reasons such as network congestion or high server load. I would recommend checking the CIS dashboard for any alerts or abnormal traffic patterns. If you suspect a DDoS attack, you may take measures including turning on \"Defense mode\" and setting your DNS records for maximum security.\nuser: What do you mean by turning on \"Defense mode\" ?",

}
